title: Hybrid priority-lane load-shedding policy and admission-control prototype
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Goal: design and ship a hybrid 'priority-lane' load-shedding and admission-control subsystem that gracefully degrades request handling under resource pressure while preserving SLOs for high-value tenants and critical request classes. The system should integrate with multi-region failover and existing circuit-breaker hooks and be controllable from the Console (per-tenant policies, lane weights, and emergency override).

Background: Current runtime-level shedding is coarse: global shedding thresholds and token-based rate limits cause wide blast radius during spikes and failover events. We need finer-grained prioritization and soft-degradation modes (approximate responses, cached fallback, token caps) to maintain P99 latency and high availability for critical traffic. This ticket funds a prototype admission controller + priority lanes and a rollout plan for controlled traffic experiments.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Prototype admission controller deployed to staging and can assign requests to at least three lanes (critical, standard, best-effort) based on request metadata and tenant config.
2) When node GPU utilization exceeds configured headroom, controller enforces lane admission policies and demonstrates reduced latency for 'critical' lane under >50% load in staging load test.
3) Integration with circuit-breaker: unhealthy downstream triggers lane promotion/demotion and recorded in tracing.
4) Console can adjust lane weights and emergency override toggles; changes take effect within 30s.
5) Metrics emitted: lane_admit_rate, lane_reject_rate, lane_eviction_count, lane_degrade_mode_active, and sieved SLOs per-lane; dashboards created in Grafana.
6) Run a canary in us-west-2 for 1 week with synthetic traffic; documented roll-back criteria and playbook in Confluence.
implementation_notes:
Design highlights:
- Admission controller runs as a hot path in the front proxy; decisions are cheap (single memcache + local token bucket check).
- Priority lanes: critical (lowest shedding), standard (default), best-effort (first to shed). Lane assignment keys: tenant_tier, route_tags, request_priority header, and heuristic for cached responses.
- Soft degrade modes per-lane: 1) cached-response fallback, 2) truncated token cap with summary-only responses, 3) approximate embedding path (lower-precision quantized model). Degrade modes are pluggable via runtime flags.
- Circuit breaker interplay: controller subscribes to per-node circuit state; if serving kernel is slow, auto-promote critical lane and return HTTP 202 + queued token to best-effort when safe.
- Multi-region failover: policy replicates lane configs to secondary region; admission controller exposes a region-aware headroom estimate through the routing layer to avoid cascading overload during cross-region failover.
- Safety: thresholds bounded by tenant SLA config; emergency override in Console will set weights to preserve only critical traffic.

Key trade-offs: keep controller decision path minimal to avoid added latency vs. richer signals (latency percentiles, model queue depth). Prototype chooses conservative signals (CPU/GPU utilization + local queue depth) and defers advanced predictive shedding to follow-up ticket.

Implementation tasks: front-proxy hook, memcache schema, lane config CRD, console UI knobs, metrics + dashboards, e2e chaos tests.
observability_requirements:
Emit per-lane metrics (request_count, admit_count, reject_count, latency_p50/p95/p99, degrade_mode_count). Add tracing tags: lane_id, decision_reason, headroom_snapshot. Create Grafana dashboards and SLO alert rules: per-tenant P99 latency alert, lane eviction spike alert. Log sampled decisions to BigQuery for offline analysis.
Links: Grafana draft: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/loadshed/prototype, Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELI/Hybrid+Priority+Lane+Shedding
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy to staging with synthetic traffic (scale up to 50% of prod RPS). Validate admission decisions and metrics.
2) Canary in us-west-2 (5% of production traffic) for 7 days with close monitoring of P50/P95/P99.
3) Expand to 25% if canary thresholds pass, otherwise rollback.
4) After 2 weeks and no regressions, enable regional failover-aware mode in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 with conservative thresholds.
5) Post-rollout: run a mixed traffic chaos test injecting region outage and drops and measure SLO preservation for critical lane.

Rollback criteria include: increased P99 for critical lane >20% over baseline, lane_admit_rate for critical drops >5%, or elevated error rate in API (>1%).
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: misclassification of requests into lanes can starve important traffic. Mitigation: start with tenant-tier only assignment and add route-tags gradually.
Risk: added decision latency in hot path. Mitigation: microbench front-proxy hook and keep decision path inline and cacheable.
Risk: config replication lag across regions causing inconsistent behavior during failover. Mitigation: add fallback default policies and versioned configs; console will display config age warnings.
